purpose: Independent practice of B1.3 (estimation to 200) with reinforcement of B1.4 (skip-counting). Captures formative evidence on strategy use and accuracy.
student_learning_goal: I can estimate the number of objects in a collection up to 200 using a chunk strategy and verify by counting.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can estimate the number of objects in a collection up to 200 using a chunk strategy and verify by counting.
header.character_watermark: Detective Tina Tens in the top-right corner with a striped vest and magnifying glass. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: For each jar, write your estimate. Circle the chunk strategy you would use.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Three jar scenes stacked vertically. Each ~7in × 1.5in. Each shows a jar illustration with items inside, plus an estimate line and two strategy bubbles (chunk-of-10 / chunk-of-100).

image_placeholders.description: Three jar scenes in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each scene ~7in × 1.5in. Jar 1 (small, ~40 buttons), Jar 2 (medium, ~100 marbles), Jar 3 (large, ~170 cubes). Each jar is partially transparent so the items are visible. Beside each jar: 'My estimate: ___' and two strategy bubbles 'chunk-of-10' / 'chunk-of-100'.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; three jars stacked.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P1_THREE_JARS: keywords (jar, estimate, chunk) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Jar 1: estimate ~40-50 (chunk-of-10). Jar 2: estimate ~100 (either strategy works; chunk-of-100 is faster). Jar 3: estimate ~170-180 (chunk-of-100 strongly preferred).

parts.student_instructions: Three skip-count tasks. Fill in the missing numbers.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Three Number Line strips stacked. Strip 1: by 20s starting at 0. Strip 2: by 25s starting at 50. Strip 3: by 50s starting at 0.

image_placeholders.description: Three horizontal Number Line strips in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each ~7in × 0.8in. Strip 1: cell 1 shows '0', label 'by 20s'. Strip 2: cell 1 shows '50', label 'by 25s'. Strip 3: cell 1 shows '0', label 'by 50s'. End cells pre-filled with 200.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; three strips.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P2_SKIP_LINES: keywords (number-line, skip-count) name what the lines show.

parts.student_instructions: Tina is at a hockey game with about 175 fans. How would you estimate? Draw and write your strategy.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank box (~7in × 3in) for the child to draw the hockey-arena scene and write their estimation strategy. Tina thinking-bubble icon in the top-right corner of the box.

image_placeholders.description: A blank rectangular drawing box in B&W line-art, ~7in × 3in, with light-grey solid outline. Tina thinking-bubble icon in the top-right corner of the box (~1in tall). Below the box, a 'My strategy:' line.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P3_HOCKEY_BOX: keywords (hockey, estimate) name what the box is for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Accept any plausible chunk-strategy explanation: 'I would count 1 row of seats then count how many rows there are about'; 'I would chunk 100 fans then add about 75 more'; 'I would look at 10 sections of 17 each = 170, close to 175'. Look for the child to ARTICULATE the strategy, not just guess.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw a school assembly with about 200 students. How would you estimate WITHOUT counting each student?
teacher_notes: Lesson 4 consolidation. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Watch for: (a) Part 1 Jar 3 children who circle chunk-of-10 (would take forever) — flag for chunk-of-100 reteach; (b) Part 2 Strip 2 children who count by 5s instead of 25s after starting at 50 — flag for the awkward-multiples practice; (c) Part 3 children who can't articulate a strategy and just write a number — coaching opportunity for strategy-language scaffolding.
